tickerText: [TENNIS] Nitto ATP Finals open Sunday at Inalpi Arena with doubles from 11:30 a.m., world No. 1 Alexander Zverev facing Rafael Jodar not before 2 p.m., and Ben Shelton meeting Arthur Fils to cap McEnroe Group night session • [SQUASH] Joel Makin lifted the $96,000 PSA Silver crown at the Pittsburgh Open, beating Leonel Cardenas in Sunday's final after Marwan ElShorbagy defeated Finnlay Withington for third • [BADMINTON] Kumamoto Masters Japan Super 500 finals Sunday saw Lakshya Sen rally past Koki Watanabe for men's singles while Akane Yamaguchi, Takuro Hoki/Yugo Kobayashi, and Rin Iwanaga/Kie Nakanishi took the other main titles • [PICKLEBALL] Proton Daytona Beach Open week at Pictona starts Monday with pro qualifying and senior open play after amateur registration closed, as John Lucian Goins chases a third straight PPA singles title on a 1,000-point Open • [TABLE TENNIS] WTT Contender Istanbul closes Sunday with men's and women's singles finals plus doubles medals, as Korea's Kang Dongsoo and Joo Cheonhui headline singles while Luxembourg's Luka Mladenovic and Mael Van Dessel defend men's doubles gold

newsItems.title: Turin Round Robin Starts
newsItems.excerpt: The 2026 Nitto ATP Finals begin Sunday in Turin with Heliovaara and Patten opening doubles before Alexander Zverev meets debutant Rafael Jodar and Ben Shelton faces Arthur Fils in John McEnroe Group singles.

newsItems.title: Sen Rallies In Kumamoto
newsItems.excerpt: Lakshya Sen came from a set down to beat home hope Koki Watanabe 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 in the Kumamoto Masters men's final, adding a second 2026 title as Yamaguchi and Japan's top doubles pairs swept the other Sunday crowns.

newsItems.title: Daytona Week Begins
newsItems.excerpt: The Carvana PPA Tour's Proton Daytona Beach Open at Pictona runs Nov 16-22 with pro qualifying Monday, as John Lucian Goins eyes a third straight singles win and Bright and Waters pursue their 19th straight doubles title.

newsItems.title: Istanbul Finals Day
newsItems.excerpt: Sunday at WTT Contender Istanbul crowns the remaining singles and doubles champions after Connor Green and Anna Hursey took mixed doubles Saturday, with Kang Dongsoo and Joo Cheonhui in the men's and women's singles title matches.
